premises.text: Social influences significantly impact product discovery and purchasing decisions.
premises.evidence_span: friends do help friends discover products.

premises.text: Current e-commerce experiences are solitary and focused on individual needs.
premises.evidence_span: the experience has become very solitary, almost like a chore.

premises.text: Sneak Peek provides visual proof of product popularity through social interactions.
premises.evidence_span: real people looking at real products.

premises.text: Users can see which friends have interacted with products on Sneak Peek.
premises.evidence_span: you also get to see which of your friends have peaked or looked at that product before.

premises.text: The Peek feature drops prices intelligently based on user interactions.
premises.evidence_span: every Peek drops the price for everyone peaking.

premises.text: Game mechanics like competition and urgency drive sales.
premises.evidence_span: game mechanics, such as competition and urgency, really drive sales.

premises.text: Sneak Peek has established over 100 brand partnerships.
premises.evidence_span: we are very excited to announce that we have over 100 brand partnerships.

value.text: Sneak Peek enhances product discovery and purchasing through social proof and engagement.
value.evidence_span: adds the social proof we all need to move us from discovery to purchase.

notes: Pilot learnings and user engagement metrics are excluded as traction.
